Pool depth of 5,208 SOL means a $20 ticket would see little price impact, so execution costs should sit near the low end of the range. The coin is 30 minutes old and has not dipped from its 30-minute high, which is the kind of strength a momentum buyer looks for.

The case is weak, though. The first two minutes after graduation show 5,008 SOL bought by 15 wallets, with the top five taking 99.9% and a bundle share of 1.0. That is an operator launch, not organic discovery, and the brief's own base rates put operator coins near break-even. The 3.7x return over 30 minutes is largely that launch-phase inflow, not demand that has accumulated since. The recent 155 buyers are real, but a 0.0 sell-to-buy ratio at launch means the operator's cost basis is unknown, and a single large exit could erase the recent gains. Most coins do not recover a dip, and this one has not yet been tested by one.
memos.skeptic:

The brief shows 5,007.87 SOL bought in the first two minutes after graduation from only 15 wallets, with a top-5 buyer share of 99.9% and bundle_share of 1.0. Those are the signatures of a single operator holding nearly all early supply, so one exit can drain the pool. Sellers appeared in the last 15 minutes (19 sellers, 18.06 SOL sold), and the 3,747% 30-minute return means the price is far above any organic level, leaving little buy-side depth against a 5,208 SOL pool.

A $20 ticket also faces 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs plus a 30-second execution lag, so even a modest reversal erases any gain. Skip.
